title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Same price in 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05: sales 1 and 6 vs baseline 3.2; no uplift observed. Indicates price sensitivity.

drivers.name: TikTok trend (novel driver)
drivers.evidence: No past sales data for similar viral trend; only one mention in notes. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk toward 1.0. Use cautious uplift.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 3.2. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 3.4% to $5.72, which may suppress demand, but recent weeks at same price (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show only 1–6 units (vs baseline 3.2), with no lift—suggesting price sensitivity. However, planner notes mention TikTok trend: a novel, untested driver. Past promotions show negligible noise-adjusted lift (x1.0), and post-promo dips are not significant. No evidence of carryover effect. TikTok trend is unconfirmed by sales history; treat as low-confidence signal. Adjust median down slightly for price, up modestly for trend, but shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.4 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
